study.title: 1 Corinthians 3 Spiritual Maturity, foundation in Christ and unity of the church
study.overview: Paul corrects the church of Corinth for its immaturity and rivalries around human leaders. The chapter shows that ministers are only servants; God is the one who gives growth. The church must build only on the foundation which is Jesus Christ, with care, because the work of each one will be tested. In the end, Paul calls believers to abandon pride in people and to remember that they belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.

outline.title: Immaturity and Carnal Divisions
outline.explanation: Paul says he could not speak like spiritually mature people, but as the still childish believers. The evidence of this carnality appears in the envy, quarrels and parties formed around human names such as Paul and Apollo.

outline.title: Ministers as Servants and God as Author of Growth
outline.explanation: Paul and Apollo are not lords of the faith of no one; they are servants through whom there was preaching. One plant, another watering, but only God gives growth. So everyone works together in the field and building God.

outline.title: Christ is the only foundation and the work will be tested
outline.explanation: Paul claims to have laid the foundation as a wise builder, but that foundation is only Jesus Christ. Every work upon him shall be examined in the day of trial; what is true shall remain, and he that is useless shall burn. The church is the temple of God, and profaning this temple brings judgment.

outline.title: Humility, rejection of human boastry and belonging to Christ
outline.explanation: The wisdom of this world should not be treated as superior to the wisdom of God. Paul quotes the Scripture to show that the wise men end up trapped in their own cunning and that their thoughts are empty. Therefore, no one should boast in human beings, for everything belongs to believers, and they belong to Christ, who belongs to God.

study.context: The chapter responds to a concrete problem in the Corinthian church: divisions, party preferences and excessive appreciation of human leaders. The notes show that Paul resumes the correction that began before, treating the community as spiritually immature and calling it back to the simplicity of the gospel and to the centrality of Christ.
study.theology: The text teaches that spiritual maturity is not measured by eloquence, preference for teachers or ability to judge people, but by submission to the gospel and by abandonment of envy and contention. Ministers are instruments, not sources of faith; therefore, they do not deserve devotion that is the responsibility of God. The metaphor of plantation and the building affirms divine sovereignty: God gives growth and Christ is the exclusive foundation. The church is also the temple of God, which gives dignity and holiness to the community and makes serious any action that corrupts it. The judgment on the work of God's servants shows that not all religious work has the same value; fidelity will be rewarded, while inappropriate work will be lost, although the salvation of the true believer remains bound to Christ. The closing of the chapter reverses the human logic of glory: believers already possess everything in Christ, and the main identity of the church is to belong to him.

scholarViews.insight: The Corinthians were converted believers, but their life and their way of thinking still did not reflect maturity in Christ; therefore Paul treats them as spiritual children.
Paul warns that ministers should not be divinized or placed them in the place of God; they are only servants through whom faith was received.
The whole church is called the temple of God because the Spirit of God dwells in it; therefore the divine presence among the people is what constitutes it as a temple.

questions: In what ways can I confuse attachment to leaders, preachers or styles with true spiritual maturity?
Is my way of serving the church built upon Christ as a foundation, or on the pursuit of personal recognition?
What, in practice, means remembering that everything belongs to believers, but that they belong to Christ?
study.practice: Examine your participation in the church in the light of this chapter: reject favoritism, give up comparisons with other servants of God, and evaluate whether your contribution is being made with fidelity and humility. He seek to grow beyond the spiritual zeal, dedicating himself to the central truths of the gospel and treating the community as a holy place where the Spirit dwells. When making decisions, ask them to build on Christ or just feed religious vanity.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided allow you to safely affirm the general theme of the chapter, but do not authorize broader historical details about the city or on specific situations beyond the divisions in Corinth. There are also different interpretative emphases on the image of fire in verses 12 to 15; here it was treated as eschatological proof of the quality of the work, without speculating beyond what the notes support.
